edges.fact: Coursera hosts the Sustainable Development specialization, a 4-course specialization covering the basics of sustainable development including urban planning, energy, and climate change.
Coursera's Sustainable Development specialization is offered by the University of Michigan.
edX hosts the Urban Planning and Development course, a 12-week course exploring urban planning principles including transportation, housing, and urban design.
The Urban Planning and Development edX course is offered by MIT.
FutureLearn hosts the Sustainable Cities course, a 6-week course examining the challenges and opportunities of creating sustainable cities.
The Sustainable Cities FutureLearn course is offered by the University of Leeds.

edges.target_entity_name: Urban Planning and Sustainable Development (Udemy course)
edges.fact: Udemy hosts a range of courses on Urban Planning and Sustainable Development, including courses on green infrastructure, transportation planning, and urban design.

edges.target_entity_name: The Death and Life of Great American Cities
edges.fact: Jane Jacobs wrote "The Death and Life of Great American Cities", a classic book critiquing urban planning approaches and advocating for human-scale, mixed-use development.

edges.target_entity_name: Sustainable Urban Planning: A Framework for Sustainable Development
edges.fact: Dr. Richard W. Judd wrote "Sustainable Urban Planning: A Framework for Sustainable Development", a comprehensive textbook on the principles and practices of sustainable urban planning.
Steven Cohen wrote "The Sustainable City", a book exploring the challenges and opportunities of creating sustainable cities.

edges.target_entity_name: Walkable Urbanism: A Guide to Creating Healthy, Efficient, and Economically Vibrant Cities
edges.fact: Christopher Leinberger wrote "Walkable Urbanism: A Guide to Creating Healthy, Efficient, and Economically Vibrant Cities", arguing for the importance of walkable, mixed-use development.
The Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) include Goal 11: Sustainable Cities and Communities.
Dr. Jonathan T. Overpeck teaches Coursera's Sustainable Development specialization from the University of Michigan.
Dr. Jonathan T. Overpeck is a Professor of Environmental Science and Policy at the University of Michigan's School for Environment and Sustainability.
Dr. Jonathan T. Overpeck received his Bachelor's degree in Geological Sciences from Purdue University in 1981.
Dr. Jonathan T. Overpeck earned his Master's degree in Geological Sciences from the University of Arizona in 1984.
Dr. Jonathan T. Overpeck earned his Ph.D. in Geology from Brown University in 1990.
Dr. Jonathan T. Overpeck was a Coordinating Lead Author for the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) Fourth Assessment Report.
Dr. Jonathan T. Overpeck was a Coordinating Lead Author for the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) Fifth Assessment Report (2013), specifically for the chapter on Sea Level Rise.

edges.target_entity_name: Climate Change 2007: Impacts, Vulnerability and Adaptation
edges.fact: "Climate Change 2007: Impacts, Vulnerability and Adaptation" is an IPCC report.

edges.target_entity_name: Climate Change 2007: Impacts, Vulnerability and Adaptation
edges.fact: Dr. Jonathan T. Overpeck co-authored the 2007 IPCC report "Climate Change 2007: Impacts, Vulnerability and Adaptation".

edges.source_entity_name: Climate Change 2007: Impacts, Vulnerability and Adaptation
edges.fact: The IPCC report "Climate Change 2007: Impacts, Vulnerability and Adaptation" was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 2007.

edges.target_entity_name: Paleoclimatology: Reconstructing Climates of the Quaternary
edges.fact: Dr. Jonathan T. Overpeck co-authored "Paleoclimatology: Reconstructing Climates of the Quaternary" (2013), a comprehensive overview of paleoclimatology and its applications in understanding climate change.

edges.target_entity_name: Paleoclimatology: Reconstructing Climates of the Quaternary
edges.fact: Dr. Raymond S. Bradley co-authored "Paleoclimatology: Reconstructing Climates of the Quaternary" (2013) with Dr. Jonathan T. Overpeck.

edges.target_entity_name: Climate Change and the Integrity of Science
edges.fact: Dr. Jonathan T. Overpeck and colleagues co-authored "Climate Change and the Integrity of Science" (2010), discussing the importance of maintaining the integrity of climate science.

edges.source_entity_name: Climate Change and the Integrity of Science
edges.fact: "Climate Change and the Integrity of Science" (2010) was published in the journal Science.

edges.target_entity_name: American Association for the Advancement of Science (AAAS)
edges.fact: Dr. Jonathan T. Overpeck is a Fellow of the American Association for the Advancement of Science (AAAS).
Dr. Jonathan T. Overpeck is a Fellow of the American Geophysical Union (AGU).
Dr. Jonathan T. Overpeck is a Fellow of the Geological Society of America (GSA).
Dr. Jonathan T. Overpeck received a National Science Foundation (NSF) CAREER Award.
The NSF CAREER Award is awarded by the National Science Foundation (NSF).

edges.target_entity_name: Implications of recent sea-level rise science for coastal protection
edges.fact: Dr. Jonathan T. Overpeck and colleagues authored "Implications of recent sea-level rise science for coastal protection" (2019), discussing implications of recent sea-level rise research for coastal protection and adaptation planning.

edges.target_entity_name: Sea level rise and implications for coastal erosion
edges.fact: Dr. Jonathan T. Overpeck co-authored "Sea level rise and implications for coastal erosion" (2017), examining the impacts of sea-level rise on coastal erosion.

edges.target_entity_name: Attribution of anthropogenic influence on sea level rise from 1993 to 2012
edges.fact: Dr. Jonathan T. Overpeck and colleagues used statistical analysis in "Attribution of anthropogenic influence on sea level rise from 1993 to 2012" (2015) to attribute observed sea-level rise from 1993 to 2012 to anthropogenic greenhouse gas emissions.
Dr. Jonathan T. Overpeck was the lead author of the Sea Level Rise Technical Report (2017), a comprehensive assessment of sea-level rise science and its implications for the United States.

edges.target_entity_name: U.S. National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA)
edges.fact: The Sea Level Rise Technical Report (2017) was commissioned by the U.S. National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA).
The Sea Level Rise Technical Report is referred to as the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers' Sea-Level Rise Technical Report.

edges.target_entity_name: Sea Level Rise and Coastal Impacts (SLRCI) Project
edges.fact: Dr. Jonathan T. Overpeck led the Sea Level Rise and Coastal Impacts (SLRCI) Project (2014-2017), which aimed to improve sea-level rise projections and develop adaptation strategies for coastal communities.

Dr. Jonathan T. Overpeck led the Climate and Sea-Level Rise (C&SLR) Initiative (2010-2014) at the University of Arizona, focused on understanding climate change impacts on sea-level rise and coastal adaptation.
The Climate and Sea-Level Rise (C&SLR) Initiative was based at the University of Arizona from 2010 to 2014.
The Climate and Sea-Level Rise (C&SLR) Initiative provided scientific input to the U.S. National Climate Assessment.
The Climate and Sea-Level Rise (C&SLR) Initiative provided scientific input to the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) Fifth Assessment Report.
The Climate and Sea-Level Rise (C&SLR) Initiative provided scientific input to the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers' Sea-Level Rise Technical Report.

edges.target_entity_name: Sea-Level Rise and Impacts on Coastal Ecosystems
edges.fact: The Climate and Sea-Level Rise (C&SLR) Initiative produced the report "Sea-Level Rise and Impacts on Coastal Ecosystems" (2012), assessing impacts of sea-level rise on coastal ecosystems and recommending ecosystem-based adaptation approaches.

edges.target_entity_name: Coastal Vulnerability to Sea-Level Rise: A Framework for Assessment and Adaptation
edges.fact: The Climate and Sea-Level Rise (C&SLR) Initiative produced "Coastal Vulnerability to Sea-Level Rise: A Framework for Assessment and Adaptation" (2013), a framework for assessing coastal vulnerability and developing adaptation strategies.

edges.target_entity_name: Sea-Level Rise Projections for the 21st Century
edges.fact: The Climate and Sea-Level Rise (C&SLR) Initiative produced "Sea-Level Rise Projections for the 21st Century" (2014), providing improved sea-level rise projections incorporating paleoclimate records, instrumental observations, and climate model simulations.
Dr. Jonathan T. Overpeck was a lead author of the National Climate Assessment (NCA) Technical Report on Sea Level Rise (2014).

edges.target_entity_name: Sea-Level Rise and Coastal Change Project
edges.fact: Dr. Jonathan T. Overpeck served as an advisor to the U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) Sea-Level Rise and Coastal Change Project.

edges.source_entity_name: Sea-Level Rise and Coastal Change Project
edges.fact: The Sea-Level Rise and Coastal Change Project is run by the U.S. Geological Survey (USGS).
